question: GQ-001
subject: a nightly job that reports success against a corrupt database
found_by: sweeping for the defect SHAPE found in the rebuild guard — a default that turns a broken input into a plausible answer

the_defect.behaviour: pointed at a file containing the literal text "not a database", it printed "rows total: unknown", then "no rows past the window", then "nothing to do", and exited 0
the_defect.why: the count queries return EMPTY on error; ${stale:-0} reads 0; and 0 is indistinguishable from "healthy, nothing expired"
the_defect.consequence: a cron running nightly against a damaged log reports success forever

two_of_my_own_probes_were_wrong_first.probe_1: set DB= to redirect it — the real knob is LOG_DB_OVERRIDE, so it read the REAL 9.5 GB log and I nearly recorded a hardcoded-path defect that does not exist
two_of_my_own_probes_were_wrong_first.probe_2: my first guard checked ${total} — that variable does not exist, the name is before_rows; it would have refused on EVERY run including healthy ones
two_of_my_own_probes_were_wrong_first.lesson: both were caught by checking the variable actually existed before trusting the edit

the_fix: refuse with exit 75 when the counts come back empty rather than zero, and print pragma quick_check(1) so the reason is visible
